task: 沿 REQ-20260801-01 继续推进 TUI：以手动导入理论和本地 CodeGraph 证据，闭合模型思考/回答/状态展示与快捷键发现性。
constraints: Presentation-only; preserve Answer/Reasoning line text, Markdown fence state, ANSI16/cell-width behavior, physical row cap, tool folding, queue/takeover/hold semantics.

PresentationLedger stores only bounded scalar identity/status/metrics; live, history, and static projections may share its anchor but execution graph, provider history, queue routing, and full transcript bodies remain untouched.
LineIndex must stay synchronized across UTF-8 appends and bounded-prefix eviction; no full transcript copy or second execution state machine.
Reuse existing tail_display_cells and bounded lexer; no syntect/tree-sitter, provider/MCP/graph/queue/execution changes.
Semantic rails and THINK/ANSWER/TOOL detail anchors are presentation-only; reserve their display cells before wrapping so narrow terminals cannot overflow or hide observed content.

Expanded detail may reuse the existing Markdown parser only in the modal path; preserve exact body text, alert/fence state, bounded detail sizes, search/scroll semantics, and do not add a second lexer.
Below 14 columns, retain a truthful micro legend for the active panel (navigation, expand/delete, Esc); do not repurpose Tab, which remains completion selection.

DetailLayoutCache stores only the current selected detail snapshot keyed by panel content revision, selection, and cell width; it must invalidate on live panel rebuild or resize and must not become execution state.

PanelItemsCache stores only one presentation snapshot for the active panel, keyed by panel revision, kind, query, selection, detail state, and cell width; it never stores execution, queue, or provider state.

PanelItemsCache may cache presentation-only ListItem physical heights and project a selected, height-bounded viewport window; it must remap selection locally and preserve multi-line rows without changing panel actions.
DetailLayoutCache uses Ratatui 0.29 Paragraph::line_count with Wrap{trim:false} for the actual Markdown detail widget; the width key and panel revision remain invalidation boundaries.

Busy narrow input chrome must preserve a compact Ctrl-C takeover token before optional tool-detail, reasoning, or Inspector tokens; it may compress text but may not change key routing or hide required token/effort status.
An explicit Ctrl+R reasoning expansion persists across later Answer chunks until the user toggles it or a new task clears streams; model output must not silently take back the audit view.

A held live viewport may reuse a semantic block ID plus logical-line anchor only for same-revision width/height reflow; FOLLOW, user scrolling, new stream content, and execution state remain unchanged.

Narrow idle chrome must expose the latest non-system ActivityKind tag and complete critical takeover/waiting/conclusion outcome when cell budget permits; it must not increase telemetry height or alter input routing.

Wide detail Inspector may split the existing modal into 40/60 list/detail columns only at inner width>=72 and height>=8; narrow frames retain vertical stacking, existing detail cache/scroll/Markdown paths, and all key/action semantics.

When busy and live_inspecting, narrow top chrome must show HOLD before right-clipped phase text and narrow input chrome must preserve ^C takeover plus the existing Ctrl+Space follow affordance; this is presentation-only and cannot alter key routing.

LiveHistory modal hints must keep HOLD/FOLLOW discoverable after the modal covers the underlying live chrome: use Ctrl+Space at wide hint widths and a truthful ^Space compact token while retaining Enter/Space, Delete, queue and Esc actions.

Committed multi-line reasoning must retain a visible continuation rail after leaving the live viewport; preserve the existing first-line metadata and DIM/ITALIC styling without changing reasoning text or execution state.

When busy live inspection is active at medium or wide widths, the input action rail must expose FOLLOW and takeover before optional long labels; preserve cell-width bounds and existing narrow shortcuts.
Committed Answer scrollback must expose the same explicit ANSWER channel used by live output while preserving Markdown roles and cell-width measurement.
Committed reasoning metadata must expose a compact THK channel marker in narrow terminals while retaining observed step, elapsed time, token count, continuation rail, and DIM/ITALIC styling.

Completed Markdown Answer bodies must remain bounded and recoverable after scrollback folding; /answers is presentation-only and must provide filtering plus Enter detail expansion without changing execution history.
Retained Answer detail must have a per-entry character bound with head/tail preservation and an explicit omission marker; transient native scrollback may keep the original text until flush.

Retained Reasoning history detail must have the same per-entry character bound with head/tail preservation and an explicit omission marker; the transient native reasoning commit may keep the original observed text.

Medium busy chrome at 48-63 columns may expose one bounded latest ActivityKind chip (CHK/SUM/WAIT/etc.); it must suppress duplicate live-channel labels and never displace HOLD/FOLLOW/takeover priority.

Ctrl+R/Ctrl+O/Ctrl+T remain global audit attention shortcuts while a panel is being browsed; they must not mutate panel queries or editor buffers, and must remain disabled in completion popups or panel edit fields.

Adjacent completed read_file call/result pairs may share one presentation-only batch block; each file's ordered call/path and bounded observation details remain available through expansion, and an intervening non-read tool breaks the batch.

Ctrl+A is a presentation-only Answer-history attention switch: it must open/close the bounded searchable Answer panel without interrupting execution or changing input; panel editor fields and completion popups retain precedence.

Each retained completed Answer row may carry only bounded scalar presentation metadata (step, elapsed seconds, estimated/observed tokens) alongside the already bounded body; metadata must not alter provider history, queue routing, or scrollback text.

Activity audit history remains bounded at 12 entries, preferentially evicts transient node chatter, and retains WAIT/ASK/SUM/TAKE/DONE/ERR signals with sequence numbers; this is presentation-only and must not alter execution or queue state.

If a run is interrupted or errors before `(final)`, the bounded streamed Answer may be committed exactly once to static Markdown and the unified Answer archive as PARTIAL with an explicit marker; it must remain expandable/searchable without entering completed-answer semantics or changing successful final-answer routing.
When the bounded Answer archive is full, eviction must preferentially remove an older PARTIAL row before a completed ANSWER conclusion; this is presentation-only and preserves the archive bound.

When a live Answer follows Reasoning and Tool blocks, top chrome at widths >=48 and the busy input rail at widths >=72 must retain a compact THINKING/Ctrl+R visibility affordance; tool folding and focus semantics remain independent.

When pending work exists, the input rail reserves an editor row before queue preview rows so queued intent stays above a wrapped draft; the cursor follows the visible draft tail, and tiny frames retain a truthful compact queue count without replacing editable input.

Pending queue presentation must bound both rendered rows and preview preprocessing: oversized pasted messages are truncated before wrapping, with an overflow affordance preserved; the full queued string remains untouched for execution.

Static committed Tool summaries with hidden details must retain a compact folded affordance (`Ctrl+O details`) so scrollback remains discoverable; expansion continues through the existing bounded history/Inspector path.
Static committed reasoning must retain its THK metadata and append a compact `Ctrl+R history` affordance on the first line; the existing bounded reasoning history remains the only expansion path.
Static committed Answers must retain the ANSWER rail and append a compact `Ctrl+A answers` affordance on the first line; AnswerHistory remains the only recovery/expansion path.

An empty completed tool observation must project one explicit `no output` row consistently in live output, native static commit, Inspector, and Tool History; call/standalone blocks must not claim an observation.

Retained WAIT/ASK/SUM/TAKE/DONE/ERR activity events may add one bounded presentation-only static scrollback anchor with a Ctrl+T activity affordance; the activity ledger remains the detail source and execution, queue, provider, and MCP semantics remain unchanged.

Compact bottom telemetry may style provider/model, context, input/output tokens, effort, and total labels as semantic spans, but must preserve the exact compact string, cell width, wrapping height, custom status templates, and telemetry values.
Metric and Label roles are reserved for telemetry hierarchy; do not reuse them to recolor user commands, model output, tools, warnings, or approval semantics.

Prominent input and device-auth surfaces use the same rounded border grammar as interactive list, completion, Inspector, and approval surfaces; this is render-only and must preserve cell geometry, cursor placement, wrapping, overlay order, and all key/execution semantics.

Audit panel titles use the same semantic channel role as their rows: Answer/Live stay primary, Reasoning/Tool/Activity/Queue stay informational; this changes title styling only and must not alter panel selection, filtering, detail expansion, or key routing.

ChromeRail owns only top-chrome display-cell accounting and bounded insertion; top_chrome remains the sole owner of semantic priority and must preserve safety/channel/HOLD/queue/reasoning/activity/status ordering, exact text, ANSI16 roles, and width bounds.

LiveFramePlan owns only live-surface measurement: bounded queue preview, input/output token and effort status projection, wrapped status height, and four-slot geometry; draw_with_cache consumes this immutable plan and keeps painting/interaction semantics separate.

draw_input_surface owns only wrapped editor rendering, sticky pending-intent projection, rounded input framing, and cursor placement; it must consume the planned queue preview without mutating queue/input/execution state.

draw_live_output owns only cached bounded-tail painting plus transient phase-anchor and breathing-cursor decoration; draw_audit_overlays owns only read-only panel/device-auth overlays; neither may own execution or interaction state.

Partial Answer native scrollback must retain the ANSWER rail and expose a bounded PARTIAL marker derived from PresentationLedger status; do not mutate Answer body text, history, successful final semantics, queue, takeover, or execution.

Idle THK result-card detail must reuse the live width-aware Reasoning contrast policy: retain italic channel separation, drop DIM only at <=40 columns, and leave Answer/SUM roles, card geometry, text, keys, queue, takeover, and execution unchanged.

flush_commits may coalesce presentation-only wrapped CommitBlock lines before the existing bounded insert_before batches, but must retain block order, separators, folding, sanitization, cell-width behavior, Viewport::Inline, and all input/queue/HOLD/FOLLOW/takeover/execution semantics.

TODO snapshots may enter the existing bounded Activity/scrollback projection as PLAN anchors; retain the execution-owned todo values, expose bounded detail through Ctrl+T, and do not add a second task state machine or alter routing.

If a graph returns normally without an `(final)` message, retain any already-streamed Answer through the existing bounded PARTIAL archive before clearing live streams; inspect only AgentState.messages, never fake completion, and preserve provider/graph/queue/execution semantics.

When a live channel coexists with an actionable lifecycle ActivityKind, expose only its bounded CHK/SUM/ASK/ERR badge in the existing full title and HOLD anchor; do not add rows, per-block borders, new focus state, or alter Tab/Enter/approval/takeover routing.

User-facing help must advertise every global audit shortcut that input_action already supports; empty-state feedback must describe recoverable Answer history, including PARTIAL entries, without changing key routing.

Audit panels own the complete supplied overlay viewport: clear it before rendering an inset modal so narrow gutters cannot leak live/idle rows; preserve existing panel geometry, detail scrolling, and all key/action semantics.

Panel metadata prefers whitespace-boundary wrapping and hard-wraps only unbroken tokens; semantic rails repeat on every continuation row, and no execution, queue, focus, or panel geometry semantics may change.
At medium AnswerHistory widths, preserve the actionable `Enter expand` and `Esc close` affordances in one bounded hint; keep LiveHistory HOLD/FOLLOW wording unchanged and do not alter panel routing.

When a wide idle input title would clip the final reasoning/activity actions, compact only lower-priority submit/newline/tab labels; keep `Ctrl+R history`, `Ctrl+T activity`, live prefixes, queue/takeover, cell bounds, and input routing truthful.
failed_knowledge: NLM proposed a whole virtualized layout layer and O(k/n)/2ms claims; CodeGraph shows the live viewport is already bounded and cached. The measured remaining gap was reverse line scanning plus full code lexing for a single long visible line, so the smaller existing presentation boundary was strengthened instead.

NLM's latest global-height-cache direction is still broader than the measured surface: the live tail is physically bounded, while static modal list wrapping was rebuilt every redraw. The local fix is a one-panel snapshot cache, not a second whole-document layout state machine.

NLM's global virtualization recommendation has now been narrowed to a measured Phase 4A boundary: active modal ListItems use cached physical heights and a selected viewport window; full transcript virtualization remains unproven and is not added.

NLM's sidebar-culling proposal does not map to the current inline four-slot layout; the measured narrow gap was missing busy Ctrl-C takeover discovery, not a real sidebar or telemetry allocation failure.

NLM's semantic anchored reflow proposal is broader than needed: existing LiveBlockFocus/LineIndex/LiveOutputCache make a presentation-only preferred anchor sufficient. Do not add a whole-document physical layout index or vertical telemetry redesign without a measured defect.

NLM's latest vertical-telemetry recommendation returned no sources_used/citations; local 32/40-column frames already preserve compact token/effort status. The measured defect was activity outcome clipping in top_chrome, not bottom telemetry height.

NLM's latest virtualized viewport/Adaptive Splitting proposal returned no sources_used/citations and its full-transcript/performance premise is unverified; current bounded live projection already protects the hot path. The locally justified slice is adaptive wide Inspector presentation, not a second global layout engine.

NLM's latest panel-culling/syntax-highlighting proposal returned no sources_used/citations and mismatched local geometry: Inspector is a covering modal, not a height-consuming sidebar, while live_markdown_spans_with_alert already reaches bounded code_line_spans/code_token_role coloring. Do not hide the user's live Inspector or add a second highlighter without a measured defect.

NLM's cited semantic-phase-rails recommendation overlaps existing live_rail/live_phase_marker/live_phase_anchor/live_inspection_chip surfaces. Local narrow-frame measurement found only a real HOLD discoverability gap: compact_busy_phase clipped a trailing HOLD marker and compact busy input omitted FOLLOW; fix by prefixing HOLD and exposing the existing Ctrl+Space as ^Space, without adding a new shortcut or state machine.

NLM's latest uncited narrow-panel-culling proposal assumes Inspector consumes responsive live height; CodeGraph shows draw_with_cache allocates the four live slots first and draw_panel_with_cache later paints a modal_rect overlay. The measured gap was the LiveHistory panel_hint hiding HOLD/FOLLOW after overlay; retain modal inspection and add width-tiered Ctrl+Space/^Space guidance.

NLM's current logged-in query returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (error code 8); authentication was already valid, so no new NLM conclusion was accepted. Local CodeGraph found static multi-line reasoning lost its continuation rail after the first `┊` line; the measured fix adds `│` to later logical lines only.

NLM remained rate-limited on the next query. CodeGraph found medium busy input_chrome put `Alt+End follow` after long labels, so right clipping could hide FOLLOW while HOLD remained visible; the local fix uses a bounded priority rail only during live inspection.

A short-timeout 32-column PTY matrix can report an isolated partial when the follow snapshot is sampled during the raw ConPTY timing window; 15-second reruns observed the same hold/follow/reasoning state, so do not treat one timing partial as a render regression. Stabilize the probe before using it as release evidence.
The latest same-session NLM query still returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (error code 8); valid login plus the user's no-research-status boundary means no new NLM conclusion is accepted.

The wide idle input title clipped `Ctrl+T activity` to `Ctrl+T activi…` after reasoning history existed; preserve both recovery actions with an adaptive presentation-only legend rather than adding a new input protocol or renderer.
Static Markdown Answer scrollback folds after 20 lines and CommitBlock::Markdown is then discarded; without a bounded history surface, long final conclusions cannot be searched or expanded.
Answer history's eight-entry bound did not bound one entry's size; retaining an arbitrarily large final response would undermine long-session TUI memory stability.

The latest same-session NLM activity query returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (error code 8); no research_status query or re-authentication was performed. CodeGraph showed medium 48-63 busy chrome lacked a stable semantic latest-activity chip, so the local measured slice adds one with HOLD priority.

Panel routing consumed Ctrl+R/Ctrl+O as query characters whenever a non-editing panel was open, making the promised thinking/tool audit shortcuts context-dependent; fix at the input boundary with a presentation-only attention dispatch.

Consecutive read_file call/result pairs remained separate ToolBlocks, so file-heavy investigation output consumed one live/history row per file; group only completed adjacent read observations and retain each bounded detail payload.
Reasoning history was bounded only by entry count; each retained entry could still carry the full 32K-character live cap, unlike AnswerHistory's 8192-character head/tail projection.
Completed Answer history was recoverable through /answers but had no global keyboard path; relying on command discovery made post-completion audit slower and left Ctrl+R/Ctrl+O/Ctrl+T asymmetrical.

AnswerHistory rows exposed only ordinal and character count; multiple long-running conclusions could not be tied to observed superstep, elapsed time, or token telemetry without reopening unrelated scrollback.

The five-entry Activity ledger could evict waiting, conclusion, approval, takeover, completion, or error evidence during long node chatter; local retention test justified a bounded prioritized eviction policy.

Static-only partial Answer retention still folded long interrupted output after 20 lines without a user-accessible expansion/search path; reuse the existing bounded Answer archive instead of creating a second history surface.
A naive FIFO Answer archive bound could evict a completed conclusion while retaining recoverable PARTIAL output; prefer PARTIAL eviction when the bounded archive is saturated.

The top chrome previously suppressed the THINKING/Ctrl+R affordance whenever any live Tool block existed, so a live Answer could hide the available reasoning inspection path; preserve the affordance alongside folded tools.
The 72–95-cell busy input rail previously omitted Ctrl+R whenever tools existed; full labels overflowed before Alt+↑/↓ focus, so use bounded ^Enter/^C/^R/^O tokens until the 96-cell full tier.

The pending queue preview was allocated only from unused input rows, so a long wrapped draft could hide queued intent and leave the cursor outside the visible editor window; reserve the queue first and project the cursor-near draft tail.
Pending queue output was capped at three rows but `wrap_input` still scanned the full queued string every redraw; one huge pasted intent could also append a fourth overflow row.
Static committed Tool blocks were collapsed and recoverable through history, but their scrollback summary gave no visible indication that details existed or that `Ctrl+O` could reveal them.
Static reasoning scrollback exposed THK metadata but gave no visible indication that the same reasoning was retained and expandable/searchable through `Ctrl+R`.
Static Answer scrollback exposed the ANSWER rail but gave no visible indication that long/folded conclusions remained recoverable through `Ctrl+A`.

Empty tool observations previously left the summary as a successful-looking blank tail and gave Inspector/Tool History an empty detail, so completion could not be distinguished from missing presentation data.

draw_with_cache previously mixed queue/status measurement, responsive slot allocation, live-tail painting, input cursor placement, and overlay rendering in one monolith; the measured architectural gap is presentation coupling, not a missing execution state.

The editor slice was still coupled to live orchestration: queue-row reservation, CJK cursor math, input chrome, and draft viewport were interleaved with status and overlay rendering; isolate them at draw_input_surface without duplicating input state.

After measurement and editor extraction, draw_with_cache still interleaved cached live-tail decoration and audit overlays; isolate those rendering responsibilities while preserving cache reuse, modal precedence, and snapshot timing.

The latest same-session NLM lifecycle-closure proposal returned sources_used:[] and empty citations; CodeGraph shows existing live rails and static closure already cover the proposed container boundary. The concrete local gap was narrower: the first /help branch omitted Ctrl+R/Ctrl+O and the no-answer feedback said completed although PARTIAL history is recoverable; the accepted slice updates presentation text only.

The latest same-session NLM lifecycle-closure follow-up again returned sources_used:[] and empty citations. Dev ConPTY at 40 columns reproduced an AnswerHistory modal leaking the underlying DONE/ANS projection through its inset gutters; clear the complete audit viewport before painting the existing modal, rather than adding per-block borders or a second renderer.

The latest same-session NLM hanging-indent/highlighter recommendation returned sources_used:[] and empty citations. CodeGraph already showed same-cell continuation rails and bounded visible-tail highlighting; Dev ConPTY instead reproduced 18-column AnswerHistory metadata splitting inside words, so the local slice adds word-boundary panel wrapping with hard-wrap fallback.

The latest same-session NLM KKP recommendation returned sources_used:[] and empty citations and conflicts with local evidence: Ctrl+Space HOLD is presentation-only, matched key releases are intentionally discarded by the current Windows-compatible input filter, and the terminal does not request REPORT_EVENT_TYPES. Do not change HOLD/FOLLOW into a momentary release protocol without a reproduced defect; the measured local gap was the medium AnswerHistory hint, fixed by preserving `Enter expand` and `Esc close`.

The next same-session NLM query returned Google error code 8 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED before an answer; it yielded no new recommendation or source evidence, so local TUI conclusions remain unchanged and no retry/status query is justified.

records.title: TUI 视觉、交互与展示层迭代
records.markdown:
### REQ-20260801-01 · TUI 视觉、交互与展示层迭代

- 批准依据:`批准`
- 状态:`ACTIVE`
- 版本:`v0.2.0`
- 行为:`RidgeCode TUI 以清晰、科技感强且终端主题友好的界面呈现实际收到且允许展示的模型输出与最终回答；Answer 与实际 reasoning_content 分层呈现，不伪造隐藏推理；模型回复、调查结论、等待/执行状态与当前 Agent 活动须持续可见，长内容先展示摘要并可展开查看有界详情；文件读取与工具输出默认合并为可折叠摘要，展开时显示有界、按终端宽度换行的有效细节；支持有界、无外部解析依赖的行级 Markdown 展示（bold、code、header）与 ANSI 16 色语义角色；关键交互可发现、可操作，长任务期间保持响应并允许用户取消当前执行后接管输入；底部状态区明确区分输入 token 与输出 token；忙碌时待提交消息粘性显示于输入框上方，Enter 追加至队尾，Ctrl+Enter 立即推至队首且不打断当前模型回合。`
- 边界:`范围限于 crates/agent/src/tui 及其直接交互/渲染依赖、展示状态模型、布局、事件处理、渲染与测试，以及按迭代门进行的 NotebookLM 架构/业界方案调研与本轮 Note 清理。不改变 langgraph 核心语义，不把具体 LLM/MCP SDK 耦合进 TUI，不牺牲安全门、确定性验证、跨平台终端兼容或数据完整性，不升级无关依赖；保留 maker/checker、权限门、危险命令拦截、输入排队/取消、事件驱动主环、Viewport::Inline、insert_before 原生 scrollback 与 ANSI 16 色主题适配方向；不覆盖 samples/config.json 与 test_codegraph.ps1。工具摘要须保留，工具详情默认折叠且有界；Markdown 仅作展示层解析。`
- 验收:`通过 cargo fmt --all --check、cargo test --workspace、cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings；TUI 纯逻辑测试覆盖 Markdown span、语义色角色、折叠/展开、状态迁移、窄终端布局、CJK/emoji 宽度、长行物理换行、Ctrl+R/Ctrl+O、输入/输出 token 分栏、Agent 活动状态、取消后接管与待提交队列预览/队首推送；证明静态提交文本无 ANSI 逃逸残留、文件读取/工具详情默认折叠且展开不越界、LiveTranscript 64 块上限有效；完成真实终端或可复现渲染验收，证明长输出按宽度换行不刷屏、模型回复/调查结论/等待/当前活动可见、摘要可展开、工具默认收起且可展开、待提交消息不遮挡当前输入，Enter/Ctrl+Enter 不打断当前回合，Ctrl-C 可交还输入控制，且单帧刷新无明显卡顿；NotebookLM 建议经 CodeGraph、当前代码与测试核验后方可落地。`
- 追踪:`REQ → crates/agent/src/tui/*.rs 的状态/事件/渲染符号 → crates/agent/src/tui/tests.rs 与 workspace 质量闸；NLM 建议证据存于 .iteration/notebooklm-response.json；Note 清理以本轮迭代 ID、闭环证据与本地 archive 记录为准。
